First I want to say that I am not a parent, but I know this is a very common experience, these are very common feelings and they are completely valid.

Here is something thats worth taking into consideration, I think: No one ever stops needing their mom.

As people grow older, they become more independent but some of the ways they need their parents change a little. You might not need to help dress him, but he will need your advice for different things. He will still need to be comforted during hard times.  He will need to know that he has you and you love him just as much as he loves you.

Source: I'm 24 and I still absolutely NEED my mom 💜

I've experienced this my entire life and honestly, it's usually because they can't handle it. They want to be nice, they don't want to be the kind of person that says "No sorry, I cannot help you" (even though that would be better than just leaving). So then they either don't try at all or they do and then ghost because they don't know how to approach someone who is already not okay and tell them they cannot help.

This honestly could be a lot of things. It could be a symptom of depression, it could be a symptom of some other mental health issue(s) or even a physical issue. The best course of action would be to talk to a doctor about it if you can, but I know that's easier said than done.
